analysis.one_liner: ABB India makes and sells electrification gear (switchgear, panels, power distribution equipment) and industrial automation/motion systems for factories, infrastructure, utilities and data centres; it is 75%-owned by the Swiss-Swedish ABB Group and exited its robotics business in 2026.
tags: Robotics unit sold to group co.
analysis.whats_happening: ABB India reports results for the July-September 2026 quarter on 13 November 2026, about four weeks away. The last reported quarter (April-June 2026) showed record order inflow of ₹4,363 crore (+50% YoY) and revenue up 21% YoY to ₹3,559 crore, alongside a ₹90-per-share special dividend funded by proceeds from selling its robotics business to a fellow ABB Group entity. The company also named a new CFO (effective January 2027) on 6 October 2026.
analysis.plain_terms: This is the Indian listing of the global ABB engineering group, selling electrical equipment and automation systems that go into factories, power grids and buildings. It just sold its robotics division to a sister ABB company, which handed the books a one-time accounting gain of about ₹1,658 crore in the January-March 2026 quarter. That gain makes recent profit and the headline valuation look different from the ongoing business: strip it out and the company's 'real' profit multiple is well above the ~48x that shows up on screens. The underlying story is strong order growth but a core profit margin that has barely moved despite much higher sales.
analysis.quarters: Profit figures over the last five quarters are not straightforwardly comparable. Jul-Sep 2025: PAT ~₹440.5 crore (+21% YoY) on revenue ~₹2,912 crore. Oct-Dec 2025: PAT ₹432.85 crore (down ~18% YoY) on revenue ~₹3,557 crore. Jan-Mar 2026: reported PAT jumped to ₹1,783.7 crore, but ₹1,658.5 crore of that was a one-off gain from slump-selling the robotics business to a group subsidiary (ABB Robotics India) for ~₹1,568 crore cash consideration - recurring profit that quarter was actually only around ₹125 crore, notably weak. Apr-Jun 2026: PAT back to ~₹362-370 crore (+3-8% YoY) on record revenue of ₹3,559 crore (+21% YoY), with core EBITA margin up only 20 basis points to 13.0% despite the strong revenue growth - several brokerages flagged this as margin pressure, not improvement. Management's commentary across calls has centred on record order intake (data centres, renewables, infrastructure) rather than margin expansion.
analysis.performance_read: No demerger or spin-off share distribution is involved here (the robotics unit was sold for cash, not demerged to shareholders), so the price series does not need adjusting for missing spin-off shares. On raw price: the stock is 22.7% below its June 2024 peak of ₹8,796 but has rallied 32.6% over the last year (vs Nifty -9.5%) from a 52-week low of ₹4,618. Over 5 years it has returned 284.6% against the Nifty's 25.3% and peer Siemens's 179.1% - a genuinely strong long-run outperformer. But the most recent 3 months show it lagging both the Nifty (-4.9%) and Siemens (-0.5%) at -8.3%, and the 3-year return (63.4%) trails Siemens (74.0%) - the very long-run numbers flatter a recent stretch of underperformance.
analysis.valuation_read: At ~48-49x trailing earnings and ~15x book value, the stock is priced for a high-quality, debt-free compounder - and it is expensive on an absolute basis even against capital-goods peers (sector median P/E is reported closer to 36x). Why it looks 'only' ~48x rather than higher: trailing EPS includes the ~₹1,658 crore one-off robotics-sale gain booked in the January-March 2026 quarter. Strip that non-recurring item out of trailing earnings and the multiple on the ongoing, core electrification-and-automation business is meaningfully higher than the headline 48-49x. Whether that premium is justified depends on whether the order-book surge converts into margin expansion, not just revenue growth.
analysis.growth_read: Growth right now is volume-led, not margin-led. Order inflow is up 50% YoY and revenue up 21% YoY in the latest reported quarter, driven by data centre, renewables and infrastructure demand - order backlog stood at a record ₹11,900 crore with no slow-moving orders. But operating (EBITA) margin moved just 20 basis points to 13.0% in that same quarter, and multiple analyst notes describe margin as 'squeezed' or 'eroding'. In a business like this, rapid top-line growth without matching margin gains is less durable than growth where both move together.
analysis.health_read: Balance sheet risk is essentially absent: debt-to-equity is reported at just 0.02, i.e. the company is effectively debt-free. The real question is business risk, not financial risk - specifically whether the core electrification/automation margin can hold up as revenue scales, since the recent quarters show volume growth outpacing margin improvement. Cash conversion from profit to free cash flow was not independently verified in this review - check on Screener for operating cash flow versus reported PAT, especially excluding the one-off robotics gain.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter ABB Asea Brown Boveri Limited (the global ABB Group) holds roughly 75% with zero pledging reported - a clean, stable controlling shareholder. Institutional ownership is modest (FIIs ~2.4%, DIIs ~9.8%). No marquee independent investor stands out in the public shareholding data reviewed - this is a classic MNC-promoter-controlled stock rather than one with well-known value investors on the register. Worth flagging: the robotics business was sold via a related-party transaction to another ABB Group entity; minority shareholders approved it by postal ballot (94% in favour), but the pricing of intra-group deals like this is always worth independent scrutiny rather than taking the gain at face value.
strengths: Record order backlog of ₹11,900 crore as of mid-2026, described as having no slow-moving orders
Order inflow up 50% YoY (₹4,363 crore) in the April-June 2026 quarter, led by data centre, renewable and infrastructure demand
Debt-to-equity of just 0.02 - effectively debt-free balance sheet
Revenue growing 21% YoY in the latest reported quarter even before the order backlog is fully executed
watchpoints: Headline trailing P/E (~48-49x) and ROE/ROCE (22.4%/30.2%) are inflated by a ~₹1,658 crore one-off gain from the robotics business sale booked in Jan-Mar 2026 - the 'real' recurring multiple is higher than it looks
Core operating margin has barely moved (+20bps to 13.0%) despite 21% revenue growth, with analysts flagging margin squeeze/erosion in recent quarters
TTM dividend yield of 1.76% is propped up by a one-time ₹90/share special dividend tied to robotics-sale proceeds (paid Aug 2026); the recurring dividend is much smaller
Stock is still 22.7% below its June 2024 peak and has underperformed both the Nifty and peer Siemens over the last 3 months, despite the strong 1-year and 5-year numbers
analysis.one_thing: The July-September 2026 results due 13 November 2026 - the first full quarter without robotics and after the special dividend - will show whether core Electrification & Automation margins recover toward historical levels or stay compressed, resolving whether the order-book surge is actually converting into profit growth.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly PAT and revenue figures were cross-checked across Business Standard, Upstox, FreePressJournal, Equitybulls and Investing.com; sources use inconsistent fiscal-year vs calendar-year labelling for the same quarter (e.g. 'Q4 FY26' = Jan-Mar 2026 = 'Q1 CY2026' in some outlets), which was reconciled manually. The exact recurring (ex-exceptional) trailing EPS and P/E were not independently recomputed - check Screener for a clean quarter-by-quarter PAT excluding the robotics-sale gain. Valuation ratios (P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE, debt/equity) are sourced from aggregator sites as of early-to-mid October 2026 and may shift slightly with the official last_close of ₹6,801 supplied.
